title: The derivatives clearing landscape in the euro area three years after Brexit
summary: Three years after Brexit, euro area CCPs achieved modest market share gains in euro-denominated clearing services. Eurex Clearing's global market share in euro-denominated OTC interest rate derivatives rose from 14% (2019) to 19% (December 2023), while LCH SA's share in euro-denominated CDS more than doubled from 24% to 42% following ICEU's CDS service closure. However, euro area CCPs remain a minority, with UK-based LCH Ltd holding 81% of OTC IRD clearing.
key_points: As of December 2020, approximately 80% of euro area OTC derivative positions were still cleared through UK CCPs, primarily LCH Ltd and ICEU
Eurex Clearing's global market share in euro-denominated OTC IRD increased from 14% (2019) to 20% (2021) and stabilized at 19% by December 2023
LCH SA's market share in euro-denominated CDS grew from 24% to 42% between 2019 and 2023, driven by ICEU's phase-out of its CDS operations
Eurex Clearing has negligible presence (<1%) in exchange-traded STIR (three-month EURIBOR futures), with silos between trading venues and CCPs cited as a contributing factor
Eurex Clearing holds a relatively high market share (32%) in euro-denominated FRAs, attributed to continued use of reformed EURIBOR alongside risk-free rates
Three euro-denominated clearing services are considered of substantial systemic importance: OTC IRD, OTC CDS, and ETD STIR
why_it_matters: The concentration of euro-denominated derivatives clearing in UK-based CCPs creates systemic risk for EU financial stability. This analysis tracks progress toward the EU's Capital Markets Union goal of reducing reliance on third-country clearing infrastructure. The modest gains by euro area CCPs suggest the transition will be gradual, and the persistent dominance of LCH Ltd means EU financial stability concerns remain relevant.
market_structure_context: This source provides detailed analysis of post-Brexit clearing landscape evolution for three systemic euro-denominated derivatives segments: OTC interest rate derivatives (IRD), OTC credit default swaps (CDS), and exchange-traded short-term interest rate derivatives (STIR). Key CCPs analyzed include Eurex Clearing, BME Clearing, LCH SA (euro area) and LCH Ltd, ICE Clear Europe (UK). The source documents how Eurex's 2018 incentive program and ESMA's recognition decision contributed to market share gains, while ICEU's CDS service closure accelerated LCH SA's growth. The analysis notes that clearing activity is concentrated mainly in euro-denominated trades, potentially limiting appeal for multi-currency portfolio clients.
important_numbers: 80% of euro area OTC derivative positions cleared through UK CCPs (December 2020)
LCH Ltd market share: 81% of OTC IRD (December 2023)
Eurex Clearing IRS market share: 8% (2019), 18% (2021), stable at 18%
